advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tie the asserted pandoc version to the pinned wheel (or acknowledge in a comment that the pandoc-version line is unverifiable and only the wheel pin is drift-guarded).
evidence: tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py:49: `assert "3.6.1" in text, "NOTICE must name the bundled pandoc VERSION, not just the component"`
NOTICE:15: `Version:    3.6.1` — a manual literal, not derived from the pin
pyproject.toml:180: `wiki = ["pypandoc-binary==1.15"]` and NOTICE only correlates 3.6.1↔1.15 in prose (docs/adr/0095: `pypandoc.__version__ == "1.15", bundled pandoc 3.6.1`) with no automated check
ABSENCE: no assertion links '3.6.1' to 'pypandoc-binary==1.15'; test_notice_and_the_pin_cannot_drift_apart only checks the wheel pin string, not the pandoc version
advisory.finding: The pandoc executable version '3.6.1' — the actual subject of the GPL/source-availability obligation — is asserted only as a hardcoded string literal and is never tied to the pinned wheel, so a pin bump to a wheel bundling a different pandoc leaves NOTICE's stale 'Version: 3.6.1' passing the test: the precise silent-drift the change claims to prevent is left unguarded for the version that matters most.
scenarios: Someone bumps pypandoc-binary to a version bundling pandoc != 3.6.1; NOTICE's Version line is not updated
The pandoc version drifts from the shipped binary while the test suite stays green

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle the two-declaration case explicitly so divergent pypandoc-binary pins produce a clear message rather than a set-unpack ValueError.
evidence: tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py:69: `(pin,) = _declared_pins()` unpacks a set expecting exactly one element
advisory.finding: `pypandoc-binary==1.15` is declared twice in pyproject.toml (the `wiki` extra and the dev/CI dependency); `_declared_pins()` dedups via a set, so if the two declarations ever diverge, `(pin,) = _declared_pins()` raises an unhandled ValueError and test_the_wheel_is_pinned_to_exactly_one_version reports 'pinned to more than one version' — a real intra-pyproject inconsistency surfaced as an ugly unpack error / misleading message rather than a clear one.
scenarios: A maintainer bumps the wiki extra but forgets the dev dependency at line 254 (or vice versa)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Parse pyproject.toml with a TOML parser (or tolerate whitespace around '==') so a whitespace-formatted pin is not misread as unpinned.
evidence: The regex is also applied to the raw file text, so a pin written across whitespace or in a commented example would be mis-parsed
ABSENCE: no TOML parsing; the assertion depends on exact `==` adjacency
advisory.finding: `_PIN_RE` matches only `pypandoc-binary==<version>` with no surrounding whitespace; TOML permits `pypandoc-binary == 1.15`, which the regex would not match, causing test_the_wheel_is_pinned_to_exactly_one_version to fail with 'a range is not a pin' even though the wheel is correctly pinned.
scenarios: A reformat or lint tool inserts spaces around '==' in pyproject.toml

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bind the recorded pandoc version in NOTICE to an authoritative source (e.g. pypandoc's reported pandoc version, or a single declared mapping) rather than asserting a hardcoded '3.6.1' literal duplicated between NOTICE and the test.
evidence: assert "3.6.1" in text, "NOTICE must name the bundled pandoc VERSION, not just the component"
_PIN_RE = re.compile(r"pypandoc-binary==([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.]*)") — the drift test binds only the WHEEL version (1.15), not the pandoc executable version (3.6.1)
NOTICE:15 'Version:    3.6.1' and NOTICE:22 'pypandoc-binary==1.15' are two distinct version numbers

docs/adr/0095-dc-segmenting-wiki-renderer.md:56 '`pypandoc.__version__ == "1.15"`, bundled pandoc **3.6.1**' — the wheel-to-pandoc-version mapping is exactly what a pin bump changes and what goes unverified

The docstring's stated threat ('a pin bump quietly leaves the recorded version describing a binary nobody distributes') covers the pandoc version, but no assertion ties '3.6.1' to any authoritative source of truth
advisory.finding: The pandoc executable VERSION (3.6.1) recorded in NOTICE is asserted only against a hardcoded string literal duplicated in the test, with no binding to the wheel pin the drift test protects. A pypandoc-binary pin bump that ships a different pandoc version can drag the '1.15' mention (caught by test_notice_and_the_pin_cannot_drift_apart) while leaving the '3.6.1' provenance line in NOTICE stale — the exact silent drift the story claims to prevent — and the suite stays green because both NOTICE and the assertion hardcode 3.6.1.
